emil_principles_description: Rules repeated across the collection that most strongly shape how an interface feels.
emil_principle_1_body: Motion should explain space, state, feedback, or a jarring change. High frequency shrinks the motion budget; keyboard actions should feel instant.
emil_principle_2_body: Enter and exit use strong ease-out, movement uses ease-in-out, and most UI stays below 300ms. ease-in feels slow at the moment of input.
emil_principle_3_body: Popovers originate from triggers, drags carry velocity, boundaries add friction, and transitions reverse from the current visual position.
emil_principle_4_body: Prefer transform and opacity. Reduced motion removes disruptive movement while preserving useful opacity or color feedback.
emil_install_description: Upstream already ships as a Markdown bundle with no runtime dependencies. Install it through skills.sh so support files such as STANDARDS.md, PLAN-TEMPLATE.md, RECIPES.md, and CATALOG.md are included.

david_overview_chain_description: Upstream does not ship one official pipeline like Matt. The repo is category-based building blocks. The chain below is this guide's recommendation so the skills can be used end-to-end: set context → capture decisions → research if needed → verified execution → sustain sessions and review.
david_overview_chain_step_1: setup-help guides setup one step per response; before-building instantly surfaces the 1-3 consequential choices in a proposed build.
david_overview_chain_step_2: ask-then-build asks the non-obvious questions one at a time, then writes a build prompt; adr-verbatim records decisions as concise ADRs.
david_overview_chain_step_3: deep-research runs cited research through DeepAPI (optional: varied-search, deep-scrape).
david_overview_chain_step_4: Long, verifiable work → goal-loop (4-part contract + validation command) with anti-sleep. Ordinary work → normal session, isolated with git-worktree.
david_overview_chain_step_5: total-review before shipping; handoff when context fills; effective-agent-skills when authoring skills.

david_overview_problem_1_description: Agents start building before the consequential choices are made; assumptions slip in silently.
david_overview_problem_2_description: Research with built-in tools yields uncited answers; no cost cap or idempotency.
david_overview_problem_3_description: Agent loops run without validate commands, constraints, or done criteria.
david_overview_problem_4_description: Full sessions without state handoffs; several agents colliding in one working directory.

david_flow_node_capture: ask-then-build: 3-6 non-obvious questions one at a time (options A-D + a pick), then a build prompt for another agent. adr-verbatim: records the decision as a concise ADR.
david_flow_node_research_gate: Branch: does the decision need structured external evidence?
david_flow_node_research: deep-research: DeepAPI POST /v1/research/deep, builds a self-contained prompt and saves a cited Markdown report. Requires a paid DeepAPI key.
david_flow_node_work_gate: Branch: is there a verifiable stop condition and a validation command? No minimum task duration applies.

david_flow_node_session: Normal interactive work; git-worktree isolates parallel tasks (one task = one worktree = one agent session).
david_flow_node_handoff: handoff: compresses the session into state (not orders): DONE / PARTIAL / NOT STARTED, why, and traps. Saved to a file and pasted into a fresh session.
david_flow_node_author: effective-agent-skills: anatomy, progressive disclosure, anti-patterns, testing, and security when writing SKILL.md.
david_workflows_description: Concrete scenarios composing David's skills. Step order is a guide recommendation — take the subset that fits.
david_workflow_1_description: A fuzzy idea needs its hidden choices surfaced and decided before an agent builds.
david_workflow_1_why: One question at a time (options + a recommendation) stops the agent silently assuming scope and edge cases; an ADR preserves the decision.
david_workflow_2_description: Stateful, multi-session learning in a dedicated workspace.
david_workflow_2_why: teach keeps the reason for learning (MISSION.md) and compressed reference notes in the workspace so lessons build across sessions.
david_workflow_3_description: Turn a research need into a cited report instead of guesses.
david_workflow_3_why: One DeepAPI call with a cost cap (maxCostUsd) and an Idempotency-Key; the result is saved with its source URLs.
david_workflow_4_description: Migrations, coverage lifts, refactors with a test contract.
david_workflow_4_why: goal-loop needs Objective, Constraints, Validation command, and Stop condition; anti-sleep prevents the Mac sleeping mid-loop.
david_workflow_5_description: Two independent reviewers, one deduplicated shortlist (needs the bb harness or an equivalent).
david_workflow_5_why: total-review keeps only real issues, marks which reviewer found each, and never fixes anything before you approve the shortlist.
david_workflow_6_description: Session almost full or focus changed.
david_workflow_6_why: State handoffs (done/partial/not-started + why + traps) beat imperative checklists.
david_workflow_7_description: Codify a repeatable workflow into a SKILL.md, then place it in every agent.
david_workflow_7_why: effective-agent-skills covers anatomy, progressive disclosure, anti-patterns, and testing; distribute-skill-to-all-agents places it in all five agent locations.
david_concepts_description: Principles that make David's skills fit a personal agent stack — more than a file dump.
david_concept_1_body: Upstream groups skills into five categories. Users assemble their own workflows. This guide only recommends the most common chain.
david_concept_2_body: Skills load name+description first (~100 tokens), body on match, references/scripts on demand. Install many skills without permanent context bloat.
david_concept_3_body: Every goal needs an Objective, Constraints, a Validation command, and a Stop condition. Also say what to read first and add checkpoints. Do not prefix the contract body with /goal, and forbid reward-hacking (deleting or weakening tests). Without these, autonomous loops become expensive drift.
david_concept_4_body: 28 of the 57 skills set disable-model-invocation: true: the agent runs them only when you invoke them (/skill-name). The rest can trigger automatically from their description. Catalog badges follow the upstream frontmatter.
david_concept_5_body: Write what is true / partial / missing; capture why and dead ends. The fresh agent chooses actions after verifying files — not from an imperative checklist.
david_concept_6_body: Compatibility + risk separate "exists on GitHub" from "fits your stack". Many skills assume the author's tools or paths (bb, cmux, Cloudroom, DeepAPI): fill in placeholders and verify prerequisites before installing.

overview_build_chain_description: This is the main pipeline from idea to merge-ready code. Each step produces an artifact that becomes the input for the next step. The entire system is designed to keep the agent in the "Smart Zone" — the window (~150k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply.
overview_smart_zone_description: A large context window (1M+ tokens) doesn't mean all of it is equally useful. The Smart Zone is the window (~150k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply; quality drops beyond it. The entire skill system is designed to keep the agent in the Smart Zone, with a phase-boundary decision between phases of work.

workflows_description: Common scenarios and recommended skill sequences. Each workflow is designed to keep the agent in the Smart Zone (~150k tokens).
workflow_1_description: Main pipeline from idea to merge-ready code (and a retrospective).
workflow_1_why: Each step produces an artifact that becomes the input for the next. No step can be skipped without sacrificing output quality.
workflow_2_description: Systematic debugging with 6 phases — feedback loop FIRST, hypothesis SECOND.
workflow_2_why: Jumping to hypothesis without a feedback loop is failure mode #1. Phase 1 (build feedback loop) is THE SKILL — the rest is mechanical.
workflow_3_description: Identify shallow modules and deepen them gradually.
workflow_3_why: If the codebase is garbage, AI produces garbage. Fix the output first, THEN improve the system that produces it. Upstream suggests running it every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: the chosen candidate enters the main flow via /grill-with-docs.
workflow_4_description: Turn a messy backlog into agent-ready work via state machine.
workflow_4_why: Without triage, issues pile up without clarity. The state machine ensures each issue has exactly one category + one state — no ambiguity.
workflow_5_description: Shortcut for small features where scope is 100% clear.
workflow_5_why: Not every feature needs a full spec. If scope is small and can be described in 1-2 sentences, go straight to grill → implement.
workflow_6_description: Handoff → prototype in new session → handoff back learnings.
workflow_6_why: When grilling finds questions that need code to answer (UI that must be seen, state machine that must be tried), don't pollute the current session. Use a fresh session's full context window to explore, compress learnings, pass back.
workflow_7_description: Carry context across via a portable markdown file.
workflow_7_why: /handoff is narrow: use it only when swapping harness (Claude → Codex), moving to a new directory/repo, sending work to a colleague, or forking a side task mid-phase. What it buys is portability: a file that travels. If nothing is travelling, you don't need it.
concepts_description: Mental models underlying this skill system.
concepts_deep_shallow_p1: The agent carries no memory between sessions — it re-reads your codebase every time. So the shape of the codebase (deep vs shallow modules) heavily determines how easily an agent can work in it; that is the point of /improve-codebase-architecture and /codebase-design (testability and AI-navigability).
concepts_deep_shallow_p2: Deep module = lots of implementation behind a simple interface. Shallow module = interface almost as complex as its implementation. With deep modules, AI can read interface types and understand what a module does — without digging into implementation.
concepts_grey_box_description: Deep modules create natural seams. You own the interface, AI owns the implementation. Tests keep it honest. You can look inside if you want — to apply taste, influence outcome, or improve performance — but as long as tests pass, you don't NEED to care.
concepts_progressive_description: Give every module its own folder with a clear public interface. AI can see all services in the file system, read their types, and understand what they do — without digging into implementation. Interface on top, details inside. The result is lighter cognitive load: you don't have to hold hundreds of interrelated modules in your head.
concepts_smart_zone_p1: Modern coding models boast 1M+ context windows. But there is a sweet spot: early in the window, attention relationships aren't strained and the agent reasons sharply. The Smart Zone is the ~150k-token window (on state-of-the-art models); past it, quality starts to degrade — the 'dumb zone'.
concepts_compact_description: Compress the current context and seed a fresh session with the summary. The default at a phase boundary, not the first reach; don't compact mid-phase or the agent loses the thread.
concepts_handoff_description: Write a portable markdown file. Narrow: only for a new harness, a new directory, a colleague, or a side task forked mid-phase. What it buys is portability.
concepts_vertical_description: Every issue must cut ALL layers end-to-end (UI → API → DB → Tests). Never break work horizontally — that creates handoff problems and partially finished work that can't be verified.
concepts_horizontal_note: → Handoff problems, partially finished work, nothing verifiable until step 4
concepts_vertical_note: → Each slice includes schema+API+UI+tests, independently verifiable
concepts_tracer_label: ← one tracer bullet cuts all layers →
concepts_afk_description: AFK (away from keyboard) = the agent can run on its own; HITL (human in the loop) = a human must be present. Upstream, these terms appear in wayfinder ticket types (Research = AFK; Prototype and Grilling = HITL; Task = HITL or AFK) and in triage's ready-for-agent label ("ready for an AFK agent").
concepts_afk_text: Agent can implement without further human input. Spec is clear enough, no unresolved design decisions. Prefer this mode.
concepts_hitl_text: Agent needs a human checkpoint — design review, architectural decision, or unresolved judgment call. Can't be left to run alone.
concepts_afk_note: /to-tickets gives each ticket blocking edges. Any ticket whose blockers are done sits on the frontier — several agents can work them in parallel.
concepts_seams_description: Seam = public interface where behavior can change without editing in place. Interface IS the test surface — callers and tests cross the same seam. If you need to test private implementation, the module boundary is wrong.
concepts_leading_description: Start every instruction with the most important word — a compact concept from pretraining that anchors behavior. One token replaces a paragraph. Examples: "tight" loop (not "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" loop), "red-green" (not "write test first then implement"), "tracer bullet" (not "thin vertical slice that proves a path works end-to-end").
concepts_context_description: Keep GLOSSARY.md as a glossary only — vocabulary definitions, not narrative or spec. ADRs only for decisions meeting 3 criteria: hard to reverse + surprising without context + real trade-off. Prototypes: fold the validated decision into the real code and keep the prototype itself as a primary source on a throwaway branch out of main. Every file in context must earn its place.

installation_notes_skills_sh: Copies editable skill files into your project; nothing updates behind your back (pull upstream changes with `npx skills update`). The CLI detects your agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, etc.) and installs skills to the right location. Upstream: the installer lets you choose skills, so make sure setup-matt-pocock-skills is one of them.
david_install_notes_skills_sh: Install directly from upstream via skills.sh. The upstream README has no install instructions, so this command uses the general skills.sh CLI. Many skills are personal/vendor-specific — check prerequisites and catalog compatibility before a bulk install.
concepts_phase_boundaries_description: A phase boundary is the gap between two phases of work (e.g., grilling done → starting implementation). At each boundary, evaluate top-to-bottom — the first 'yes' wins:
concepts_pb_continue: Stay in session if the next phase needs earlier context as a primary source & fits in the Smart Zone (~150k).
concepts_pb_clear: Empty context window when the next phase is self-contained (e.g., between independent tickets).
concepts_pb_handoff: Write state to portable Markdown when changing directories, harnesses/agents, or handing to a colleague.
concepts_pb_subagent: Delegate a tightly-scoped subtask to an isolated context window and receive a consolidated report.
concepts_pb_compact: Default fallback: compress session in-place at intentional breaks when verbatim history is disposable.
workflow_8_description: Agent hits credential setup, third-party dashboard steps, or critical one-off migrations.
workflow_8_why: /wizard generates an interactive bash script; the human runs it locally to fill .env/secrets securely without leaking credentials into chat history.
workflow_9_description: Technical or domain decisions blocked by information held only by someone else.
workflow_9_why: /to-questionnaire grills you about the send, drafts an async Markdown questionnaire for the stakeholder, and feeds answers back into /grill-with-docs or /to-spec.
emil_preview_emil_design_eng_before_desc: Example anti-patterns: 500ms duration, ease-in, scale(0) entrance from center, button without press feedback.
emil_preview_emil_design_eng_after_desc: Per emil-design-eng: 160ms duration, strong ease-out cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), scale(0.95) + opacity entrance from the trigger origin, active:scale(0.97) press feedback.
emil_preview_apple_design_before_desc: Disconnected drag: no pointer capture, stops dead upon pointer release without momentum, boundary hits hard wall.
emil_preview_apple_design_after_desc: Apple direct manipulation: pointer capture active, velocity momentum projected with spring settle, rubber-band resistance at both boundaries.
emil_preview_vocab_before_desc: Vague intuition from designer/PM that causes guesswork and mismatched implementations.
emil_preview_vocab_after_desc: Glossary term: 'Scale in' (grows from smaller to full size, often with a fade), distinguished from 'Pop in' (slight overshoot).
emil_preview_opportunities_before_desc: Over-animation: animating every single element regardless of frequency, creating UI noise.
emil_preview_opportunities_after_desc: Emil's frequency gate: rejects high-frequency nav/hover elements. Only approves modal entrance with clear spatial purpose.
emil_preview_review_before_desc: Example of what gets blocked: transition all, ease-in on UI, scale(0) entrance, and a layout property animated.
emil_preview_review_after_desc: Passes review: only transform and opacity, under 300ms, strong ease-out, scale(0.95) + opacity entrance.
emil_preview_audit_before_desc: Chaotic motion: inconsistent easings and durations scattered across the app with no shared tokens.
emil_preview_audit_after_desc: Structured audit by category: findings are ranked HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW and produce self-contained plans under plans/.

jakub_overview_question: Why use Jakub Krehel's specialized skills?
jakub_overview_answer: AI often produces 'almost right' UIs that feel unpolished: nested radii that aren't concentric, icons off their optical center, numbers without tabular figures. These skills give concrete rules per domain (accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color, UI polish) and one orchestrator that combines them into a single ranked report.

brooklyn_overview_answer: Portable SKILL.md packages with no harness-specific commands, hooks, or adapters. Focused on real shipping: a polished diff (clean), a shaped and linked PR (pr-update, cpr), CI and review threads cleared (pr-ready, babysit), and maintainer triage. Some run automatically through defaults.md.
superpowers_hero_description: A complete software development methodology for coding agents by Jesse Vincent: three-path brainstorming (Spike, Bounded, Architectural), bite-sized plans, Subagent-Driven Development (SDD), TDD, and code review. Skills are triggered automatically by a plugin bootstrap.
superpowers_overview_question: How does Superpowers keep agents on track?
superpowers_overview_answer: The agent does not jump into code: it discovers intent, writes a spec and plan, then executes task by task with TDD and review. In SDD each task goes to a fresh implementer subagent that does not inherit the session history, with a progress ledger on disk. Skills trigger automatically through the using-superpowers bootstrap.

workflow_10_title: Parallel Build of a Whole Spec
workflow_10_description: /implement-spec reads the tickets as a task graph and runs parallel subagents onto one integration branch.
workflow_10_why: The alternative to /implement per ticket: you orchestrate the build instead of driving each ticket. Implementer subagents work in their own worktrees across the frontier, a merger subagent folds them into the integration branch, then one /code-review runs over it.

overview_chain_1: Relentless interview (/grilling + /domain-modeling) → shared understanding + GLOSSARY.md glossary + ADRs
overview_chain_2: Synthesize (NO re-interview) → spec with user stories, decisions, out-of-scope
overview_chain_3: Break spec → tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges (one file per ticket under .scratch/, or tracker)
overview_chain_4: Per ticket via /implement (or the whole spec via /implement-spec): Red→Green via /tdd at seams; refactoring goes to code-review
overview_chain_5: Two-axis: Standards (Fowler smells) ∥ Spec (matches spec/ticket?). Then /pr and /retro.

jakub_flow_review: Change review (diff, branch, PR): resolves the scope, reads both sides of the diff, classifies findings (Introduced / Regression / Pre-existing), then hands the review to better-interface.
jakub_flow_bi: Orchestrator: routes the interface through the six domain skills in order, collects their evidence, and consolidates one ranked report (at most 15 findings). It cannot start interface-review itself; it asks the user to run it.
jakub_flow_a11y: Domain 1: semantic HTML, keyboard and focus, accessible names, forms, assistive technology.
jakub_flow_layout: Domain 2: spatial grouping, alignment, spacing, responsive structure, logical CSS properties.
jakub_flow_writing: Domain 3: source wording, terminology, tone, labels, errors, and empty states.
jakub_flow_typo: Domain 4: text rendering, type scale, font behavior, wrapping mechanics, tabular numbers.
jakub_flow_colors: Domain 5: palette structure, color tokens, notation, gamut, rendered-pair contrast measurement.
jakub_flow_ui: Domain 6: optional visual polish: surfaces, icons, and motion once the underlying interaction is sound.
jakub_flow_verdict: One ranked findings table (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) with file:line evidence, coverage, verification, and the verdict.
jakub_flow_variant: Builds three intentionally different UI versions along one axis behind a picker on the real page; the decision is handed to the user.
jakub_flow_break: Renders one real component on a temporary page for each relevant scenario; observes what broke and names the domain skill that owns the fix.
jakub_flow_explain: Explains how a site or an effect was built, with every claim tagged Measured / Derived / Inferred.

jakub_lab_description: Try two rules from the better-ui skill: concentric radius and optical alignment. This is an illustration, not an official upstream tool.
jakub_lab_radius_body: For closely nested elements, the outer radius must equal the inner radius plus the padding between them. The same radius on both layers looks off. Past 24px of padding, treat the layers as separate surfaces and choose each radius independently.
jakub_lab_past_24: Padding past 24px: treat as separate surfaces.
jakub_lab_optical_body: A play icon is a triangle: its geometric center is not its visual center. better-ui suggests shifting it slightly right (translateX(2px) on the glyph). This example applies to the play glyph; other asymmetric icons are best fixed in the SVG itself.
brooklyn_defaults_body: defaults.md is a small set of baseline behaviors meant to be always loaded, not invoked. Append it to ~/.hermes/SOUL.md (Hermes Agent), your AGENTS.md (Claude Code, Codex, and most agents), or ~/.cursor/rules/defaults.mdc (Cursor, alwaysApply: true). It points to skills: e.g. clean before any PR handoff, ui-only and ui-system for UI work, work for a dedicated worktree, pr-ready and babysit for CI/reviews, and the rule to always link PR/MR numbers with the full URL.
brooklyn_install_description: The upstream-documented install: give your agent the repo URL and ask it to copy each skills/<name>/ directory as a complete unit, so references and bundled resources stay intact. There are no harness-specific commands, hooks, or setup scripts.
brooklyn_install_agent_note: Name one skill, a few, or all of them; the agent places them where its harness expects. Just name the skill in the sentence; the leading slash is only shorthand and does not depend on slash-command support.

brooklyn_install_hermes_note: On Hermes Agent you can skip copying: clone the repo and point at it, so git pull is the update path and every skill shows up as a slash command.
